name: Scoring, movement and hits live in plain exported functions
instruction: State changes in a game, such as scoring, moving and hit detection, MUST live in exported functions that take and return plain data and never touch the canvas, the DOM, `window`, `document`, `requestAnimationFrame` or `performance.now()`. `start` calls those functions and only draws and wires up input. It fails when the loop in `start` or an event handler adds to the score, moves things or checks for a hit itself, or when an exported logic function reaches for the DOM or the clock. Water cannon's `createState`, `fire`, `press`, `step`, `isHit` and `scoreForHit` must pass.
relevant_when: The file is a game's `game.ts`. Return not applicable for test files.
context: Vitest is the only test runner, and the cloud machine can't run browser tests, so logic written inside start can't be tested at all. House rule 4 in AGENTS.md.
scope_reason: The logic functions and start sit in the same game.ts.

checklist.name: no-state-logic-in-start
checklist.rule: start and its handlers don't compute score changes, positions or hits inline; they call exported functions for that.

checklist.name: logic-is-browser-free
checklist.rule: Exported functions other than start don't touch the canvas, the DOM, window, document, requestAnimationFrame or the wall clock; time comes in as a parameter such as dt.

references.note: House rule 4: game logic is testable without a browser.
